name: Hanging Leg Raise
summary: A calisthenics core exercise performed by hanging from an overhead bar and raising straight legs to horizontal or above through hip and lumbar flexion.

setup: Grasp the pull-up bar with an overhand grip roughly shoulder-width apart.
Hang at full arm extension with your shoulders actively depressed and your core engaged to prevent swinging.
steps: Keeping your legs straight and feet together, contract your abdominals and hip flexors to raise your legs forward.
Continue raising your legs until they are at least parallel to the floor, actively rounding your pelvis upward to engage the lower abdominals.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement under full control.
Lower your legs slowly back to the starting dead-hang position without swinging.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you raise your legs toward horizontal and inhale smoothly as you lower them.
cues: Tuck your tailbone toward your chest at the top

common_faults.fault: Using momentum and swinging the torso to kick the legs up
common_faults.correction: Reset to a complete dead hang between reps and lift with muscular control rather than momentum.

common_faults.fault: Only flexing at the hips without curling the pelvis upward
common_faults.correction: Ensure your pelvis tilts posteriorly at the top to fully contract the rectus abdominis.

precautions: Ensure your grip is secure on the bar before initiating the movement.
Bend your knees slightly if hamstring tightness pulls your lower back excessively.
